title: Snowball Valley
principle: Power of compounding; consistency brings wins; SIP discipline; lump sum vs periodic
product: SIP, index fund, recurring deposit, PPF
philosophy: Time in the market beats timing the market

lessons.title: Interest on interest
lessons.subtitle: The snowball effect
lessons.capability: Explain compounding and the Rule of 72.

steps.speaker: kip
lines: Welcome to Snowball Valley! Here's my favourite idea in all of money.
When your interest earns interest, money snowballs. That's compounding.

steps.title: Simple vs compound
steps.caption: ₹10,000 at 10% a year. Drag the years.

predict.question: ₹10,000 at 10% a year for 20 years. Simple interest gives ₹30,000. Compound interest gives…
predict.reveal: About ₹67,000, more than double simple interest, because interest keeps earning interest.

steps.question: What makes compound interest different from simple interest?

options.why: Same rate! The difference is what the interest is paid on.

options.text: You earn interest on past interest too
options.why: Exactly. Each year's interest joins the pile and starts earning too.
Compounding works on ₹100 just like on ₹1 crore.

steps.question: Rule of 72: at 12% a year, money doubles in about…

options.why: Yes! 72 ÷ 12 = 6. A handy shortcut for compounding.
That's at 6% a year (72 ÷ 6 = 12).
Divide 72 by the rate: 72 ÷ 12 = 6 years.

steps.title: Compounding in real life
steps.realLife: Banks compound FD interest, often every quarter. Investments like index funds compound when gains stay invested and keep growing.

lessons.title: Time is the secret ingredient
lessons.subtitle: Start early beats start big
lessons.capability: Explain why starting early beats starting big.

steps.speaker: dash
lines: I'll start investing at 25. I'm a teen, what's the rush?

steps.speaker: kip
lines: Let's run the numbers, Dash. Same ₹1,000 a month, same returns. Only the starting age changes.

predict.question: Starting at 15 vs at 25 (both stop at 60). How much more does the early starter end with?
predict.reveal: About 3×! Ten extra years at the start means ten more years of snowballing at the end.

steps.question: Why does starting early matter so much?

options.text: Early money compounds for the longest
options.why: Yes. The first rupees you invest get the most years of snowballing.

options.text: Markets go up more for young people
options.why: Markets don't care how old you are. Your edge is time.
Amount matters, but time multiplies everything. Early beats big.

steps.question: Aarav invests ₹1,000 a month from 15 to 25, then stops. Dash invests ₹1,000 a month from 25 to 60. At a hypothetical 12%, who has more at 60?

options.why: Surprise! Aarav's early money had 45 years to snowball.

options.text: Aarav, even though he invested far less
options.why: Yes! Aarav ends with about ₹1.5 crore from ₹1.2 lakh invested. Dash ends with about ₹65 lakh from ₹4.2 lakh. Hypothetical numbers, real lesson.
Not even close. Time in the market makes the difference.

steps.title: Teens can start
steps.realLife: In India, a minor can invest in mutual funds through an account in their own name, operated by a parent or guardian.
steps.mission: Work out how many years you have until you turn 60.

steps.speaker: kip
lines: Big lump sums are rare for teens. But a small amount every month? You can do that.
That's a SIP: a Systematic Investment Plan. Same amount, same date, every month.

steps.brief: Snowball Run! Coins in a row grow your snowball. SIP gates bank your coins. Avoid CASH OUT ramps: they reset the snowball.

options.why: That's a lump sum. A SIP is small and regular.

options.text: Investing a fixed amount at regular intervals
options.why: Yes: fixed amount, fixed date, automatically. Discipline on autopilot.
A SIP is a way of investing, usually into a mutual fund.

steps.question: Why can a SIP build wealth even with small amounts?

options.why: No market investment guarantees returns. SIP returns still go up and down.
There's no bonus. The power comes from consistency and time.

options.text: Consistency plus compounding over many years
options.why: Exactly. Small amounts, every month, for years, then the snowball takes over.

steps.title: Cards unlocked: SIP + Index Fund
steps.realLife: Many Indians run SIPs into index funds that track the Nifty 50, India's 50 biggest listed companies. Index funds are low-cost and diversified, but their value swings in the short term.
steps.deeper: Mutual funds need KYC: PAN, Aadhaar-based verification and a bank account. A minor's folio is opened in the minor's name with a parent or guardian, and moves to the child's own KYC at 18.

lessons.title: Lump sum vs SIP
lessons.subtitle: All at once, or bit by bit?
lessons.capability: Compare lump sum and SIP investing.

steps.speaker: dash
lines: I got ₹12,000 for my birthday! Should I invest it all today, or ₹1,000 a month for a year?

steps.speaker: kip
lines: Honest answer: it depends on what the market does next, and nobody knows that.

steps.title: Same money, three markets
steps.caption: Pick a market. The same total is invested either way.

steps.question: When does a lump sum usually beat a SIP?

options.text: When prices rise steadily after you invest
options.why: Right. All your money rides the whole rise from day one.
Then the SIP wins: it keeps buying at lower prices.
Not always. It depends on the market path, which nobody can predict.

steps.question: Prices fall for a year, then recover. Why does the SIP do better?

options.why: Fees are the same. It's about the price you buy at.

options.text: It keeps buying more units while prices are low
options.why: Yes! That's rupee-cost averaging: the same ₹1,000 buys more units when prices dip.

options.text: The SIP is protected from falls
options.why: SIP values fall too. They just buy cheaper on the way down.

steps.title: Card unlocked: Lump Sum
steps.realLife: Both beat leaving money idle. Many investors with a lump sum split it into a few monthly instalments to reduce timing regret.
steps.deeper: A Systematic Transfer Plan (STP) parks a lump sum in a low-risk fund and moves a fixed amount into an equity fund every month: a lump sum and a SIP in one.

lessons.title: Don't break the snowball
lessons.subtitle: Why in-and-out hurts
lessons.capability: Explain why consistency beats taking money in and out.

steps.speaker: dash
lines: Every time my investment goes up a bit, I take it out and buy something. Smart, right?

steps.speaker: kip
lines: Oh, Dash. Every withdrawal restarts your snowball from scratch.

steps.title: Steady vs in-and-out
steps.caption: Both invest ₹500 a month for 20 years. Dash cashes out every 4 years.

predict.question: Kip invests ₹500 a month for 20 years. Dash does the same but cashes out everything every 4 years. Dash ends with…
predict.reveal: About 30%! Each withdrawal knocked the snowball back to small, so it never got to grow big.

steps.brief: Resist the CASH OUT ramps! Keep the snowball rolling and bank it at SIP gates.

steps.question: Why does taking money in and out hurt your returns?

options.why: Yes. The biggest growth comes in the later years, and withdrawals keep you stuck in the early ones.
Fees can apply, but the real cost is lost compounding.
It hurts a lot. The chart showed about 70% less!

steps.title: Card unlocked: Recurring Deposit
steps.realLife: A Recurring Deposit is a monthly FD: training wheels for the habit. Banks and post offices offer RDs from about ₹100 a month.
steps.deeper: Missing RD instalments usually costs a small penalty, and banks may close the RD after several misses. Set the date just after your money comes in.

lessons.title: Boss: The long game
lessons.subtitle: Patience is a superpower
lessons.capability: Plan a long-term, consistent investing habit.

steps.speaker: kip
lines: Final boss of Snowball Valley! Let's put it all together.
Some investments even lock your money to protect you from… yourself.

steps.brief: Boss run! Longer and faster. Bank at every SIP gate and never cash out.

steps.question: PPF locks money for 15 years. Who is it good for?

options.text: Someone saving for next month's trip
options.why: Locked for 15 years, so that money won't be there next month!

options.text: Someone saving for a goal very far away
options.why: Yes. Long lock-ins suit long goals, and they stop you breaking the snowball.
Lock-ins cost flexibility, but they enforce patience. That's useful for long goals.

steps.question: Which habit builds the biggest snowball?

options.text: Invest big once, then check daily
options.why: Daily checking tempts you to react. Consistency beats intensity.

options.text: Start early, invest every month, don't withdraw
options.why: That's the whole of Snowball Valley in one sentence.
Nobody can time the market reliably. Waiting is The Melt's favourite thing.

steps.question: A friend says, "I'll invest when the market is perfect." What would Kip say?

options.text: Time in the market beats timing the market
options.why: Exactly. Being invested for many years matters more than finding the perfect day.

options.text: Good idea, wait for a crash
options.why: Crashes can't be predicted, and waiting means losing years of compounding.

options.text: Only invest after a big rise
options.why: Chasing rises is Dash's move. Steady SIPs don't need perfect timing.

steps.title: Card unlocked: PPF
steps.realLife: The PPF is a government-backed scheme with a 15-year lock-in, tax-free interest and a rate set every quarter. You can put in ₹500 to ₹1.5 lakh a year, and a parent can open one for a minor.
steps.deeper: PPF deposits can be claimed under Section 80C in the old tax regime, and the interest and maturity amount are tax-free. After 15 years you can extend a PPF in 5-year blocks.
